English සිංහල தமிழ் Fact Checked All Economy Society Environment Politics Health Methodology About Us Explore Fact-Checking Contact Us #falsenews False Post: Derana Clip Was Never on Met Dept Website False Social media posts claiming that the official website of the Department of Meteorology displayed footage from a Derana news broadcast are false. by Anonymous | December 11, 2025 Following the recent national disaster, warnings issued by the Department of Meteorology have come under heavy criticism online. Much of this backlash stemmed from an interview given by the Department’s Executive Director to Derana television. Amid this discussion, several photographs began circulating on social media, alleging that Derana’s news clip had been published on the department’s official website. These images referenced comments made by Director Athula Karunanayake on November 12th and started spreading widely from December 8th. FactSeeker examined the authenticity of these claims. The news report in question was broadcast on Derana on November 28th, highlighting the Director’s earlier remarks. Link : – https://www.youtube.com/live/ydeWAmqZFsM?t=2284s However, a review of the Department of Meteorology’s official website from November 28th to December 8th revealed that no such content had ever been published. In fact, no news material from any media organization has appeared on the website at any time. Furthermore, when contacted by FactSeeker, Director Athula Karunanayake confirmed that the department had not uploaded or shared any such news item. Therefore, FactSeeker verifies that the images circulating on social media — claiming to show Derana news footage published on the Department of Meteorology’s official website are completely false. We are an independent fact-checking team affiliated with the Sri Lanka Press Institute(SLPI). The objective and long-term goal of the FactSeeker is to provide the public with reliable and verified content in the attempt of debunking mis/disinformation. The unit, with the SLPI, is committed to contributing to improved media literacy in Sri Lanka.
